answer: Persistent History Ledger. Each agent must submit a growing chain of prior signed interactions, hashed and timestamped into a slow karst-like deposit of public checkpoints. Duplicates cannot reuse the same chain without detection, since split histories fork visibly at the checkpoint root. A copied chain is a glacier: it accrues no new depth and stalls. Honest agents seed fresh randomness each epoch, a willow regrowing from the root. Attacker cost: rebuilding months of checkpoint depth per fake identity.
